cues.text: Welcome to Study Session 4 of MIT 8101, Information Technology Management.
This session is titled IT Operations, Service and Change Management.
We begin with the first section, the learning objectives.
By the end of this session, you should be able to do several things.
First, you should understand how IT operations sustain availability, security and resilience.
In other words, you should see how the day-to-day running of technology keeps systems available to users, keeps them protected, and helps them recover when something goes wrong.
Second, you should be able to compare IT service management frameworks, looking at how the different approaches organise and govern the delivery of IT services.
Third, you should be able to measure service quality, so that you can judge whether the services an IT function provides are actually meeting expectations.
Fourth, you should be able to apply three change models: Lewin's model, Kotter's model, and the ADKAR model.
Each offers a different way of thinking about how organisations move from the way things are done now to a new way of working.
Fifth, you should be able to manage resistance, which is the reaction people often show when change is introduced.
Sixth, you should be able to plan, execute and control IT projects, covering the whole path from preparation, through delivery, to monitoring progress.
Finally, the lesson also includes a practical identity and access management audit.
This gives you a hands-on exercise in checking who has access to which systems, and whether that access is appropriate.
Keep these objectives in mind as we move through the session, because each of the topics that follow connects back to one of them.
